lower_bound_bridge.J_pattern_check: For nonorthogonal y,z, U=<y,z> is a nondegenerate plane. Two common centers force any third base x into U; distinct projective points of U are nonorthogonal, so the required related x,x' pair cannot occur.
lower_bound_bridge.K_pattern_check: An embedded K quotient would contain injected S3 patterns on both incidence sides; the odd-q Q(4,q) triad-center theorem excludes the line-side pattern.

even_q.fact: W(q) is self-dual; the point-side J-pattern obstruction therefore holds on both sides

odd_q.fact: Q(4,q), dual to W(q), has 0 or 2 centers for every triad; hence the line side has no S3-pattern

facts: W(q) is a generalized quadrangle of order (q,q)

proof_dependencies.statement: In a C4/C6-free bipartite graph, a related pair has a unique common neighbor; three pairwise related vertices share that neighbor; S_k copies correspond to independent triples with at least k common centers.
For unrelated u,v, Z_uv is independent; with minimum degree d>=2, sum over unrelated v of |Z_uv| is at least d(d-1)^3 by nonbacktracking 4-edge walks.
A maximum-cut/pruning argument produces a nonempty bipartite B of order N<=n and minimum degree d with m<=2nd and Delta(B)(d-1)^2<=N.
Convexity applied to the Z_uv counts gives, for each center u, C_u >> d^12/N^2 copies of S2 centered at u.
Excluding J makes each A_yz independent with pairwise disjoint neighborhoods, so |A_yz|<=N/d and the number T_S of independent triples with at least two centers is at most N^3/(6d).
If U is the set of vertices that are not centers of any S3, then every counted triple at u in U has exactly two centers; U4 and U5 imply |U| << N^5/d^13.
Excluding K forces U to be a vertex cover. With Delta(B) << N/d^2, Nd <= 2e(B) <= 2|U|Delta(B) << N^6/d^15, hence d^16 << N^5.
If m >= C n^(21/16), then d >> C N^(5/16), so d^16 >> C^16 N^5, contradicting U7 for sufficiently large C.
